title: How to keep candidate pipeline warm between roles on Mac: a recruiter guide
metaTitle: Keep candidate pipeline warm between roles: simple Mac recruiter workflows
description: Stop candidate ghosting and manage your follow-up cadence efficiently. Learn manual fixes and automated routines to keep your pipeline warm on macOS.
targetKeyword: keep candidate pipeline warm between roles
intro: You can keep candidate pipeline warm between roles by using a structured, multi-touch cadence that balances human connection with automated reminders. Most recruiters struggle because they rely on memory rather than a repeatable system, leading to missed touchpoints and candidate disengagement.
tldr: Use a 3 to 4 touch sequence spaced over two weeks.
Automate your bottom tier tasks to save one day of work per week.
Use a multi-channel approach including email, LinkedIn, and calls.
Define clear exit criteria for every stage to avoid manual guesswork.
Hold ⌥ ⌘ to let Lazur answer your questions while you work.

blocks.text: Why you lose candidates in the middle of the process

Top candidates are off the market in 10 to 14 days. If your hiring process takes 42 days on average, you are losing talent before you even reach the offer stage. The primary issue is administrative drag. You spend 52 percent of your day on tasks like data entry and scheduling instead of building relationships. When you lack a formal cadence, you rely on gut feeling. This leads to inconsistent communication and candidates feeling ignored.
The 3 to 4 touch rule for candidate engagement

Data shows that 98 percent of potential replies are captured by the fourth touch. Space these touches roughly one week apart. Use a shorter one-day gap between the first and second touch to establish momentum. If you only email, you risk being filtered out. Add LinkedIn messages or a quick phone call to your sequence. This feels like helpful outreach rather than pestering.
How to fix your follow-up cadence without new software

items: Create a standard template for every stage of your pipeline.
Set calendar reminders for every candidate follow-up.
Use Gmail labels to categorize candidates by their last touch date.
Define clear exit criteria so you know exactly when to stop following up.
Block two hours every morning specifically for candidate outreach.

blocks.text: If you handle regulated roles like nursing or accounting, always follow your employer rules regarding patient or client data privacy. Never store sensitive PII in public notes or unencrypted spreadsheets.
blocks.title: A note on compliance

blocks.text: Lazur helps you manage your Mac workspace so you can focus on the candidate. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about your schedule or to find a specific candidate in your browser. Lazur can draft your follow-up emails in Gmail or help you organize your tracker in Google Sheets.

faq.question: How often should I follow up with a candidate?
faq.answer: Aim for 3 to 4 touches. Start with a one-day gap, then space subsequent touches about one week apart.

faq.question: Does automation make my outreach feel robotic?
faq.answer: Only if you use generic templates. Use automation to handle the scheduling and reminders, but keep your emails personal and relevant to the candidate role.

faq.question: What if the candidate does not reply after four touches?
faq.answer: Move them to a long-term nurture list or close the file. Respecting their silence is as important as your persistence.

fixes.title: Standardize your templates
fixes.text: Create three versions of your follow-up email and save them as Gmail drafts.

fixes.title: Set hard exit criteria
fixes.text: Decide when to stop reaching out to avoid wasting time on cold leads.
